newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard to seek InkJet partners.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard to seek InkJet partners.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co will on Thursday announce the formation of a new business unit dedicated to forging partnerships for third party to exploit the use of its InkJet printing technology, executives said.

The new group, to be called the Specialty Printing Systems Operation, will report to HP's InkJet supplies business unit and will be able to build partnerships with the help of the company's strong patent portfolio and manufacturing capacity.

"HP's experience and expertise with InkJet technology uniquely position us for success in this new challenge," Dana Seccombe, general manager of HP's Inkjet supplies business unit, said in a statement prepared for the announcement.
HP has grown to be a dominant player in the InkJet market, building a market share upwards of two-thirds of the market, according to recent data provided to analysts by the company.

"Specialty printing Systems Operation is chartered to work with third parties to modify and apply HP products for new applications in markets not currently addressed by HP," the company said in a statement.

"Dramatic advances in thermal inkjet technology now provide significant opportunities to apply this technology to a wide range of complementary printing applications and markets," a spokeswoman for the company said.

Since entering the InkJet market in 1984, HP has formed close partnerships with some seleced third parties, but has not actively sought to build such ties on a broad basis until now, the company said.
With third parties, it has previously implemented projects ranging from large format textile proofers and point-of-sale transaction printers to automatic teller machines.

HP said it has previously worked with Matsushita, Sharp and Segam as well as Kodak LaserMaster Technologies, Collosal Graphics and VIP Design. In Japan, it has an agreement with NEC for distribution of co-branded printers.
An HP InkJet printer is manufactured every 1.7 seconds, according to company data.
